thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple NotReady nodes in cluster 'infer-usw-1' — 3 nodes flipped to NotReady in last 2m. Affected pods: inference-pool-usw-* (OOM / kubelet restart). Errors: scheduling failures, CrashLoopBackOff on runtime containers. Pager: pages to on-call.

maria (oncall): saw the page. Confirmed spikes in 5xx and 504s on dashboards. Latency + error rate started ~ 13:02 UTC. Customer-facing endpoints showing 10-20% request failures.

maria (oncall): @sam can you grab node logs? suspect kubelet restarts or driver crash based on earlier incidents.

sam (runtime): looking now. kubectl get nodes shows 3 nodes NotReady: infer-node-13, infer-node-21, infer-node-37. Pod count high; several inference pods restarted.

sam (runtime): running: ```kubectl describe node infer-node-37 | sed -n '1,120p'``` shows kubelet last start: "Started kubelet" 13:01:58, then taints "node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoExecute"

jake (infra): pulling journalctl on node: ```ssh infer-node-37 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80'``` — shows repeated kubelet crashes, stack traces point to container runtime failing to create device plugin for nvidia-gpus. Also kernel shows: "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" and NVIDIA UVM driver messages.

sam (runtime): driver crash => downstream runtime containers losing GPU device => pods OOM / crash loop. This matches CUDA driver mismatch or kernel bug. Any recent node image or driver pushes in the last deploy window?

jake (infra): No infra deploys in last 24h. Rolling upgrade to node image started yesterday but not on these nodes. Could be hardware/firmware flakiness or temp power glitch. Checking cloud provider health.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigation: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain pods gracefully to healthy pool 3) autoscale up inference pool to absorb load 4) failover traffic if latencies remain high. I'll start cordon/drain now.

maria (oncall): ```kubectl cordon infer-node-13 && kubectl drain infer-node-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30``` doing sequentially across the three.

sam (runtime): recommend also temporarily lowering pod antiaffinity to allow bin-packing while scaling, and enable fallback to smaller-quant models for non-critical tenants.

maria (oncall): scaling inference deployment: ```kubectl scale deployment inference-pool-usw --replicas=48 -n redwood-infer``` — kicked. Monitoring pod startup.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by maria (oncall). Escalation level: P1. Incident channel: #incidents. Public status page draft: "Experiencing elevated errors for inference endpoints in US-WEST; mitigation in progress." @marketing for status page.

nirav (sre): taking node-level handoff once initial drain done. I'll try to repro driver failure in isolated node, and AWS instance health check. Assigning to infra team for driver/firmware validation.

jake (infra): spinning temporary spare nodes with updated NVIDIA driver (535.104) and kubelet 1.29.2 to test stability. Will label them infer-usw-spare.

sam (runtime): after draining two nodes, pod failures decreased ~ 6 mins after scale up. Error rate dropped from 18% -> 3% for most customers but a heavy tenant still sees sporadic 500s (their models pinned to multi-GPU pods).

maria (oncall): customer impact: major customers A/B show degraded throughput but no full outage. Notifying sales & CS to contact any actively impacted customers.

sam (runtime): logs from runtime service show container-level OOM after GPU device removal: ```E runtime: could not init device: cudaErrorNoDevice: no CUDA-capable device is detected``` — those pods should have been rescheduled to spare nodes; investigating scheduler failures (maybe nodeSelector/taints).

jake (infra): found cloud provider returned 503 for attach/detach calls during the window; some volumes couldn't reattach which delayed reschedules. Opening ticket with provider now.

maria (oncall): next steps: - keep nodes cordoned until infra validates driver/firmware - replace affected nodes via reprovision (not reboot) - keep autoscaled replicas up for 1 hour, then evaluate scale-down policy - update incident timeline for postmortem.

nirav (sre): i'll take primary after the handoff. maria, leaving a short handover: cordoned and drained infer-node-13/21/37, scaled inference-pool to 48, spare nodes spun with updated driver, provider ticket opened. Current status: customer error rate 3% (improving), monitoring for regressions.

maria (oncall): handing off to @nirav — I have to sign off for the next shift. Full notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1748001234

nirav (sre): acknowledged, taking over. I'll coordinate with infra to repro & reprovision, and with runtime to add a temporary scheduler sanity check to prefer spare nodes. If error rate creeps >5% I'll re-escalate.

maria (oncall): thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update logged. P1 incident created: INC-2026-0421. Timeline entry added.

pagerduty: Reminder: on-call handoff performed. Pager duty notes sent to rotation.

nirav (sre): end of thread update — infra confirms hardware telemetry shows intermittent PCIe resets on infer-node-37; nodes scheduled for reprovision. Will include driver pinning in reprovision image. Closing active mitigation in ops; postmortem will cover root cause & follow-ups.
